334.text: the gentleman , examining his pocket - book

171.text: something about Dick that was attractive

562.text: Dick , who had already set to work

quotes.text: "Wake up there, youngster,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Wake up, you young vagabond!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I suppose you'd lay there all day, if I hadn't called you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What time is it?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Seven o'clock."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Seven o'clock! I oughter've been up an hour ago. I know what 'twas
made me so precious sleepy. I went to the Old Bowery last night, and
didn't turn in till past twelve."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You went to the Old Bowery? Where'd you get your money?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Made it by shines, in course. My guardian don't
allow me no money for theatres, so I have to earn it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Some boys get it easier than that,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You don't catch me stealin', if that's what you mean,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Don't you ever steal, then?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, and I wouldn't. Lots of boys does it, but I wouldn't."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Well, I'm glad to hear you say that. I believe there's some
good in you, Dick, after all."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, I'm a rough customer!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"But I wouldn't steal.
It's mean."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'm glad you think so, Dick,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Have you got any money to buy your breakfast?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, but I'll soon get some."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Shine yer
boots, sir?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How much?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Ten cents,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Ten cents! Isn't that a little steep?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, you know 'taint all clear profit,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"There's the _blacking_ costs something, and I have to
get a new brush pretty often."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And you have a large rent too,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes, sir,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I have to pay such a
big rent for my manshun up on Fifth Avenoo, that I can't afford to
take less than ten cents a shine. I'll give you a bully shine, sir."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Be quick about it, for I am in a hurry. So your house is on Fifth
Avenue, is it?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It isn't anywhere else,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What tailor do you patronize?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Would you like to go to the same one?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, no; it strikes me that he didn't give you a very good fit."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "This coat once belonged to General Washington,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"He wore it all through the Revolution, and it got torn
some, 'cause he fit so hard. When he died he told his widder to give
it to some smart young feller that hadn't got none of his own; so
she gave it to me. But if you'd like it, sir, to remember General
Washington by, I'll let you have it reasonable."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Thank you, but I wouldn't want to deprive you of it. And did your
pants come from General Washington too?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"No, they was a gift from Lewis Napoleon. Lewis had outgrown 'em
and sent 'em to me,--he's bigger than me, and that's why they
don't fit."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It seems you have distinguished friends. Now, my lad, I suppose you
would like your money."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I shouldn't have any objection,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I believe,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I
haven't got anything short of twenty-five cents. Have you got
any change?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Not a cent,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"All my money's invested in the Erie
Railroad."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "That's unfortunate."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Shall I get the money changed, sir?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I can't wait; I've got to meet an appointment immediately. I'll
hand you twenty-five cents, and you can leave the change at my
office any time during the day."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "All right, sir. Where is it?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No. 125 Fulton Street. Shall you remember?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes, sir. What name?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Greyson,--office on second floor."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "All right, sir; I'll bring it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I wonder whether the little scamp will prove honest,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"If he does, I'll give him
my custom regularly. If he don't as is most likely, I shan't mind
the loss of fifteen cents."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I guess he wouldn't want to stay long if he did get in,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Leastways I shouldn't. They're
so precious glad to see you that they won't let you go, but board
you gratooitous, and never send in no bills."
quotes.speaker: Unknown
